'''Kenneth Neil Cukier''' (born 1968) is an American journalist and author of books on technology and society. He is best known for his work at ''[[The Economist]]'' and the book ''Big Data: A Revolution that Will Transform How We Work, Live and Think'',<ref>{{cite book|last1=Cukier|first1=Kenneth|title=Big Data: A Revolution That Will Transform How We Live, Work, and Think|date=March 5, 2013|publisher=Houghton Mifflin Harcourt|location=Boston|isbn=978-0544002692|pages=256|edition=1st|url=http://www.big-data-book.com/}}</ref> coauthored with [[Viktor Mayer-Schönberger]] and published by [[Houghton Mifflin Harcourt]] in 2013.

==Career==
He has also written for ''[[The New York Times]]'', ''[[Financial Times]]'', ''[[Foreign Affairs]]'' and other publications. He was technology editor of the [[Wall Street Journal]] Asia edition in Hong Kong in 2001. In 1999 he coined the term "[[Frenchelon]]" to describe the French government's surveillance capabilities.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spies Like Us |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB9543629505575888 |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=WSJ |language=en-US}}</ref>

He teaches a course on AI and religion at the [[Woodbrooke Quaker Study Centre|Woodbrooke Centre]], a Quaker learning institute in Britain, based on talks he has given at DLD and the UN AI4Good conference in 2025.<ref>https://www.woodbrooke.org.uk/people/kenneth-cukier/
</ref> He is on the expert advisory committee of [http://AIandFaith.org AIandFaith.org], a nonprofit organization of theologians and technologists.<ref>https://aiandfaith.org/our-experts/</ref>

==Publications==

''Big Data'' was a New York Times bestseller, translated into 21 languages and a finalist for the [[Financial Times and McKinsey Business Book of the Year Award]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2013-09-18 |title=Finalists that are worthy of a bruising debate |work=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/fe6ced92-2091-11e3-9a9a-00144feab7de#axzz2fXzwqqic |access-date=2023-03-10}}</ref> The pair published a follow-on work in 2014, ''Learning With Big Data: The Future of Education''.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Learning with Big Data: The Future of Education|last=Cukier|first=Kenneth|publisher=Houghton Mifflin Harcourt|year=2014|isbn=9780544355507}}</ref> In 2021 Cukier published ''Framers: Human Advantage in an Age of Technology and Turmoil'' on the power of mental models and the limits of artificial intelligence with Mayer-Schönberger and a third coauthor, Francis de Véricourt.

==Media==
{{blockquote|"Privacy was the central challenge in a small-data era. In the big data age, the challenge will be safeguarding free will, moral choice, human volition, human agency."|Cukier. 2016. Ted Radio Hour with Guy Raz}}

In a radio interview in September 2016, Cukier described the current [[big data]] revolution as an agent of change similar to the  [[Printing press#Gutenberg.27s press|Gutenberg press]] and the [[Printing press#The|Printing Revolution]]. He cautioned that while there will be huge benefits, there is a need to have limitations in place to "preserve our fundamental freedoms" and to prevent Big Data from being another version of [[George Orwell|Orwell's]] [[Big Brother (Nineteen Eighty-Four)|Big Brother]].<ref name="Cukier_TED_2016">{{citation |url=https://www.npr.org/templates/transcript/transcript.php?storyId=492297006 |title=How Will Big Data Change The Way We Live? |date=September 9, 2016 |access-date=December 23, 2016 |work=Ted Radio Hour with Guy Raz}}</ref>

==Boards==
In 2008 he was named to the board of directors of [[International Bridges to Justice]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Board of Directors International Bridges to Justice |url=https://www.ibj.org/who-we-are/board/board-of-directors/ |access-date=2023-03-10 |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2015 he joined the board of The Open String Foundation,<ref>The Open String Foundation board of directors http://www.theopenstringfoundation.org/our-team/</ref> which provides classical instruments to disadvantaged children.

==Affiliations==
In 2016 he was elected a trustee of [[Chatham House]],<ref>Chatham House Council https://www.chathamhouse.org/about/council-and-directors</ref> a British international affairs institute. In 2017 he was named an associate fellow at Oxford University's [[Said Business School]], where he has run sessions on artificial intelligence and business.

==Awards==
He received an honorary doctorate of humane letters from [[Wittenberg University]] in Springfield, Ohio.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.publicnow.com/view/5A724D774376EC160D45ED927D657F0A8F9AC4F2?2016-05-10-21:31:05+01:00-xxx2097|title=Wittenberg University To Recognize Alumni During 2016 Commencement Exercises|publisher=Wittenberg University}}</ref>
